title: #thewildduck #henrikibsen #tfana #theatretok #theatrereview
transcript: The Wild Duck is the latest classic at Theatre for a New Audience. It's mostly about a family with skeletons in their closet that an old friend is desperately trying to release. Much of the play is spent on exposition and backstory, followed by revelations that wreak havoc on everyone involved. For a tragicomedy, I didn't find it very funny, but rather amusing in how peculiar the characters and their interactions are. This is an Ibsen play, so of course it's very psychological and raises universal questions of morality and relationships, but it felt pretty distant to me compared to some of his other works. Maybe it was the stiff translation or just the plot itself, but I couldn't invest emotionally. But that's not to say that I disliked the production — I thought it was well paced, and every actor committed wholeheartedly to the complexities and contradictions in these characters. Especially in Act 2, the themes came together and provided a debate around the inherent virtue of truth, or lack thereof. What one sees as noble and righteous behavior can be seen by another as despicable and unfathomable. And I suppose the constant inability for us humans to reach a consensus would be comedic if it weren't also so tragic. With that, another program for my collection.
